standard.title: HOROLOGY — WATCH BEZEL AND BACK COVER GAUGES — TECHNICAL SUPPLY CONDITIONS — GENERAL
standard.sector: Horology Sectional Committee, LM 23 / Light Mechanical Engineering Division Council [1]
standard.description: This Standard mainly covers the general technical supply conditions of plain and thread gauges to be used in manufacturing of watch bezels and back covers. It also recommends the material to be used in manufacturing and the markings to be provided on the gauges [2].
standard.scope: This Standard mainly covers the general technical supply conditions of plain and thread gauges to be used in manufacturing of watch bezels and back covers. It also recommends the material to be used in manufacturing and the markings to be provided on the gauges [2].

certification.description: Conformity assessment is governed under the Bureau of Indian Standards scheme, providing third-party certified material and testing parameter compliance.
requirements: Requires materials from IS 4432 : 1988 for manufacturing snap gauges, recommending chemical steel designations: 16 Mn 5 Cr 4 and 20 Mn 5 Cr 5 (typographically printed as 20Mn5CrS) [4].
The measuring surfaces of all manufactured gauges must carry a minimum hardness of 700 HV (equivalent to approximately 60 HRC) to prevent measurement face wear [4].
All completed gauges and gauge members must be thoroughly demagnetised after heat treatment to prevent magnetic attraction of debris [4].

Gauges and gauge members must be well-finished. All sharp corners and edges of measuring surfaces must be broken and free from burrs and defects. In thread gauges, incomplete starting threads must be removed and a blunt start provided [4].
Whenever grooves or recesses are provided on the gauges for colour coding, they must hold a minimum depth of 0.3 mm and a minimum width of 2 mm, with their bottom corners suitably rounded [4].
A suitable anti-corrosive coating must be applied on the finished gauges. They must then be wrapped in wax paper and packed inside cardboard, wooden, or plastic boxes [4].
Any final observed or calculated test or analysis value must be rounded off per IS 2 : 1960 to the same number of significant places as specified in the standard [5].
